1. What is a Pronoun? (Definition & Purpose)1. सर्वनाम (Pronoun) क्या है? (परिभाषा एवं उद्देश्य)

A Pronoun is a word used in place of a noun in order to avoid awkward and unnecessary repetition of the noun in a sentence or paragraph.

Example:

  • Awkward (Repeated Noun): Rahul bought a new car because Rahul loves driving, but Rahul's car broke down.
  • Natural & Correct (With Pronouns): Rahul bought a new car because he loves driving, but his car broke down.

Here, he and his replace the noun Rahul, making the sentence grammatically crisp and readable.

सर्वनाम (Pronoun) वह शब्द है जो किसी संज्ञा (Noun) के स्थान पर प्रयुक्त होता है, ताकि वाक्य में संज्ञा को बार-बार दोहराना न पड़े और भाषा सहज व सुंदर लगे।

सरल उदाहरण:

  • संज्ञा का बार-बार दोहराव (अशुद्ध/अजीब): अमन एक अच्छा लड़का है। अमन रोज स्कूल जाता है। अमन के पिताजी डॉक्टर हैं।
  • सर्वनाम के साथ (शुद्ध एवं सहज): अमन एक अच्छा लड़का है। वह रोज स्कूल जाता है। उसके पिताजी डॉक्टर हैं।

यहाँ वह और उसके सर्वनाम हैं जो संज्ञा 'अमन' की जगह आए हैं।

📌 Core Takeaway / मुख्य बिंदु:
A pronoun must always agree with the noun it replaces (its antecedent) in Person (1st, 2nd, 3rd), Number (Singular, Plural), and Gender (Masculine, Feminine, Neuter). सर्वनाम हमेशा उस संज्ञा (Antecedent) के अनुसार होना चाहिए जिसके लिए वह आ रहा है — यानी पुरुष (Person), वचन (Number) तथा लिंग (Gender) में पूर्ण सामंजस्य होना अनिवार्य है।

2. Classification: 8 Types of Pronouns2. सर्वनाम के 8 प्रमुख प्रकार

In standard English grammar tested in SSC CGL, CHSL, and CPO, Pronouns are classified into 8 core categories:

  1. Personal Pronouns: Refer to specific persons or things (I, we, you, he, she, it, they).
  2. Demonstrative Pronouns: Point out specific objects or position (this, that, these, those).
  3. Relative Pronouns: Connect dependent clauses and refer to a preceding noun (who, whom, whose, which, that).
  4. Interrogative Pronouns: Used to ask questions (who, whom, whose, what, which).
  5. Indefinite Pronouns: Refer to non-specific, vague persons or things (everybody, nobody, someone, all, few, none).
  6. Reflexive & Emphatic Pronouns: Turn the action back to the subject or emphasize it (myself, himself, themselves).
  7. Distributive Pronouns: Refer to persons or things one at a time (each, either, neither).
  8. Reciprocal Pronouns: Express mutual relationship (each other, one another).

प्रतियोगी परीक्षाओं (SSC CGL, CHSL, CPO) के दृष्टिकोण से सर्वनाम को 8 मुख्य भेदों में बाँटा गया है:

  1. पुरुषवाचक सर्वनाम (Personal Pronouns): व्यक्तियों या वस्तुओं के लिए प्रयुक्त होते हैं (I, we, you, he, she, it, they)।
  2. संकेतवाचक सर्वनाम (Demonstrative Pronouns): किसी वस्तु की ओर संकेत करने वाले (this, that, these, those)।
  3. संबंधवाचक सर्वनाम (Relative Pronouns): दो वाक्यों या उपवाक्यों को जोड़ने वाले (who, which, that, whose, whom)।
  4. प्रश्नवाचक सर्वनाम (Interrogative Pronouns): प्रश्न पूछने के लिए प्रयुक्त (who, what, which, whose, whom)।
  5. अनिश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम (Indefinite Pronouns): अनिश्चित व्यक्ति या वस्तु का बोध कराने वाले (everybody, someone, nobody, all, few)।
  6. निजवाचक सर्वनाम (Reflexive Pronouns): कर्ता पर क्रिया का प्रभाव दर्शाने वाले (myself, himself, herself, themselves)।
  7. प्रत्येकवाचक सर्वनाम (Distributive Pronouns): एक समय में एक व्यक्ति या वस्तु का बोध कराने वाले (each, either, neither)।
  8. परस्परवाचक सर्वनाम (Reciprocal Pronouns): आपस के संबंध को व्यक्त करने वाले (each other, one another)।

3. Personal Pronouns & Master Case Table3. पुरुषवाचक सर्वनाम एवं संपूर्ण कारक सारणी

Personal Pronouns change their form based on Person (1st, 2nd, 3rd) and Grammatical Case (Subjective, Objective, Possessive Adjective, and Possessive Pronoun). Understanding this table is fundamental to solving 90% of error-spotting questions in SSC.

पुरुषवाचक सर्वनाम (Personal Pronouns) के तीन पुरुष होते हैं: प्रथम पुरुष (First Person - बोलने वाला), मध्यम पुरुष (Second Person - सुनने वाला), तथा अन्य पुरुष (Third Person - जिसके बारे में बात हो रही हो)। नीचे दी गई सारणी को कंठस्थ कर लें:

Person (पुरुष) Number (वचन) Subjective (कर्ता रूप) Objective (कर्म रूप) Possessive Adjective (+ Noun) Possessive Pronoun (अकेला) Reflexive Pronoun
1st Person Singular (एकवचन) I (मैं) me (मुझे) my (मेरा + संज्ञा) mine (मेरा) myself (मैं स्वयं)
1st Person Plural (बहुवचन) we (हम) us (हमें) our (हमारा + संज्ञा) ours (हमारा) ourselves (हम स्वयं)
2nd Person Singular / Plural you (तुम/आप) you (तुम्हें) your (तुम्हारा + संज्ञा) yours (तुम्हारा) yourself / yourselves
3rd Person Singular (Male) he (वह - पुरुष) him (उसे) his (उसका + संज्ञा) his (उसका) himself (वह स्वयं)
3rd Person Singular (Female) she (वह - स्त्री) her (उसे) her (उसका + संज्ञा) hers (उसका) herself (वह स्वयं)
3rd Person Singular (Neuter) it (यह/वह - निर्जीव/जीव) it (इसे) its (इसका + संज्ञा) — (No pronoun form) itself (यह स्वयं)
3rd Person Plural they (वे) them (उन्हें) their (उनका + संज्ञा) theirs (उनका) themselves (वे स्वयं)

⚠️ Crucial Exam Distinction / महत्वपूर्ण परीक्षा अंतर:
Possessive Adjective always needs a noun immediately following it: "This is my car."
Possessive Pronoun stands completely alone without any noun: "This car is mine." (Never write mine car ✗). Possessive Adjective (my, our, your, his, her, their): इसके तुरंत बाद संज्ञा (Noun) का आना अनिवार्य है: "This is my book."
Possessive Pronoun (mine, ours, yours, his, hers, theirs): यह हमेशा अकेला आता है, इसके बाद संज्ञा नहीं आती: "This book is mine." (कभी भी mine book नहीं लिखते ✗)।

4. Demonstrative, Relative, Distributive & Reciprocal Nuances4. संकेतवाचक, संबंधवाचक, प्रत्येकवाचक एवं परस्परवाचक सर्वनाम की बारीकियां

A. Demonstrative Pronoun vs Demonstrative Adjective:

  • Pronoun (Stands alone as subject): This is my house. / Those are ripe apples.
  • Adjective (Qualifies the noun next to it): This house is mine. / Those apples are ripe.

B. Relative Pronouns (Who, Whom, Which, That):

  • Who: Used strictly for persons as Subject ("The man who helped me is my friend.").
  • Whom: Used strictly for persons as Object ("The girl whom you met yesterday is my sister.").
  • Which: Used for non-living things, animals, or for choice ("The book which I bought is costly.").
  • That: Used for both persons and things, especially after superlatives, all, same, only, none.

C. Reciprocal Pronouns (Each other vs One another):

  • Each other: Strictly used for exactly TWO persons or things. ("Both brothers love each other.").
  • One another: Strictly used for MORE THAN TWO persons or things. ("The students helped one another.").

A. संकेतवाचक सर्वनाम vs संकेतवाचक विशेषण (This, That, These, Those):

  • सर्वनाम (Pronoun): जब ये अकेले आएं: This is my pen. (यह मेरा पेन है)।
  • विशेषण (Adjective): जब इनके तुरंत बाद संज्ञा हो: This pen is mine. (यह पेन मेरा है)।

B. परस्परवाचक सर्वनाम (Each other vs One another का स्वर्णिम नियम):

  • Each other: केवल और केवल दो (2) व्यक्तियों या वस्तुओं के लिए आता है।
    उदाहरण: Both sisters respect each other. (दोनों बहनें एक-दूसरे का सम्मान करती हैं)।
  • One another: दो से अधिक व्यक्तियों या वस्तुओं के लिए आता है।
    उदाहरण: All the four players congratulated one another. (चारों खिलाड़ियों ने एक-दूसरे को बधाई दी)।

5. The 17 Golden Exam Rules of Pronoun (With Error-Spotting Examples)5. सर्वनाम के 17 स्वर्णिम नियम (परीक्षा में बार-बार पूछे जाने वाले नियम व उदाहरण)

Rule I: Verbs Followed by Reflexive Pronounsनियम 1: जिन क्रियाओं के बाद Reflexive Pronoun अनिवार्य होता है

When the subject of the verb is also the receiver of the action, the action is reflected. The following verbs are used reflexively if no direct object is present: acquit, absent, avail, reconcile, amuse, resign, avenge, revenge, enjoy, exert, apply, adapt, adjust, pride, overreach. यदि क्रिया का कोई प्रत्यक्ष कर्म (Direct Object) न हो, तो निम्नलिखित क्रियाओं के बाद Reflexive Pronoun (myself, himself, themselves आदि) का प्रयोग अनिवार्य है: acquit, absent, avail, reconcile, amuse, resign, avenge, revenge, enjoy, exert, apply, adapt, adjust, pride.

Examples (उदाहरण):

  • ✓ You should avail yourself of every opportunity in life.✓ तुम्हें जीवन के हर अवसर का लाभ उठाना चाहिए।
  • ✗ They enjoyed during the summer vacation. (Incorrect)
    ✓ They enjoyed themselves during the summer vacation. (Correct)✓ उन्होंने गर्मियों की छुट्टियों में खूब आनंद लिया।
  • ✓ He resigned himself to his failure.✓ उसने अपनी असफलता को स्वीकार कर लिया।
  • ⚡ Crucial Note on 'Enjoy': If a direct object is already given, do NOT use a reflexive pronoun!
    "They enjoyed the movie last evening." (Here 'the movie' is the direct object, so themselves is not required).     ⚡ ध्यान दें: यदि 'enjoy' के बाद कर्म (Object) मौजूद हो, तो Reflexive Pronoun नहीं आता! जैसे: "They enjoyed the picture."

Rule II: Verbs That Are NEVER Used Reflexivelyनियम 2: जिन क्रियाओं के बाद Reflexive Pronoun कभी नहीं आता

The following intransitive/reflexive verbs do NOT take reflexive pronouns: keep, stop, turn, qualify, bathe, move, rest, hide. निम्नलिखित क्रियाओं के बाद खुद को दर्शाने के लिए Reflexive Pronoun (yourself, himself आदि) लगाना पूर्णतः अशुद्ध है: keep, stop, turn, qualify, bathe, move, rest, hide.

Error-Spotting Practice Examples:

  • ✗ You should keep yourself away from bad companions. (Drop 'yourself')
    ✓ You should keep away from bad companions.✓ तुम्हें बुरे लड़कों से दूर रहना चाहिए।
  • ✗ He has qualified himself for the post of Inspector. (Drop 'himself')
    ✓ He has qualified for the post of Inspector.✓ वह इंस्पेक्टर पद के लिए योग्य हो गया है।
  • ✗ The thief hid himself behind the counter. (Drop 'himself')
    ✓ The thief hid behind the counter.✓ चोर काउंटर के पीछे छिप गया।

Rule III: Reflexive Pronouns Cannot Stand Alone as Subject or Objectनियम 3: अकेला Reflexive Pronoun कभी कर्ता या कर्म नहीं बन सकता

A reflexive pronoun (myself, yourself, himself) cannot act as the subject or object of a verb unless it is preceded by the corresponding noun or pronoun. (Colloquial use of "Myself Rahul" in spoken English is 100% grammatically incorrect in exams!). Reflexive pronoun कभी भी वाक्य का स्वतंत्र कर्ता (Subject) या कर्म (Object) नहीं बन सकता। स्पोकन इंग्लिश में बोला जाने वाला "Myself Rahul" प्रतियोगी परीक्षा में पूरी तरह गलत है।

Exam Practice Questions:

  • ✗ Myself will see to it that you get justice. (Wrong)
    ✓ I will see to it that you get justice. (Correct)✓ मैं देखूंगा कि तुम्हें न्याय मिले।
  • ✗ Yourself and he reached the venue on time. (Wrong)
    ✓ You and he reached the venue on time. (Correct)✓ तुम और वह समय पर कार्यक्रम स्थल पर पहुंचे।
  • ✗ Raj will buy books for myself and my sister. (Wrong)
    ✓ Raj will buy books for me and my sister. (Correct)✓ राज मेरे और मेरी बहन के लिए किताबें खरीदेगा।
  • ✓ I myself investigated the case. (Correct — here 'myself' is an Emphatic pronoun qualifying 'I').

Rule IV: Verb 'To Be' Takes Subjective Case Complementनियम 4: 'To Be' क्रिया (is/am/are/was/were) के बाद Subjective रूप आता है

When the complement of the verb 'to be' (is, am, are, was, were, been) is a personal pronoun, it must always be in the Subjective (Nominative) case, NOT the objective case. जब 'To Be' क्रिया (is, am, are, was, were) का पूरक कोई सर्वनाम हो, तो वह हमेशा Subjective Case (I, he, she, we, they) में आएगा, Objective (me, him, her, us, them) में नहीं।

Exam Examples:

  • ✗ It is me who have brought you home. (Wrong)
    ✓ It is I who have brought you home. (Correct)✓ मैं ही हूँ जो तुम्हें घर लेकर आया हूँ।
  • ✗ Was it her who did it for you? (Wrong)
    ✓ Was it she who did it for you? (Correct)✓ क्या वह वही थी जिसने तुम्हारे लिए यह किया?
  • ✗ If I were him, I would not accept the bribe. (Wrong)
    ✓ If I were he, I would not accept the bribe. (Correct)✓ यदि मैं उसकी जगह होता, तो रिश्वत न लेता।

Rule V: Verbs and Prepositions Are Followed by Objective Caseनियम 5: क्रिया तथा Preposition के बाद हमेशा Objective Case आता है

Whenever a pronoun follows a transitive verb or a preposition (such as between, to, for, with, except, like, let), it must always be in the Objective Case (me, him, her, us, them). किसी भी क्रिया अथवा Preposition (जैसे between, to, for, with, except, let, but) के बाद आने वाला सर्वनाम हमेशा Objective Case (me, him, her, us, them) में होना चाहिए।

Exam Traps:

  • ✗ Between you and I, Suhani is very intelligent. (Wrong)
    ✓ Between you and me, Suhani is very intelligent. (Correct)✓ तुम्हारे और मेरे बीच की बात है, सुहानी बहुत बुद्धिमान है।
  • ✗ Let they go there immediately. (Wrong)
    ✓ Let them go there immediately. (Correct)✓ उन्हें तुरंत वहाँ जाने दो।
  • ✗ She is teaching Rohit and she. (Wrong)
    ✓ She is teaching Rohit and her. (Correct)✓ वह रोहित और उसे पढ़ा रही है।
  • ✗ Everyone attended the party except he. (Wrong)
    ✓ Everyone attended the party except him. (Correct)✓ उसके अलावा सभी पार्टी में शामिल हुए।

Rule VI: Order of Pronouns (231 vs 123 Rules)नियम 6: सर्वनामों का क्रम (231 और 123 का नियम)

When pronouns of different persons are used together in a single sentence, their sequence is strictly governed by etiquette and context: जब एक ही वाक्य में अलग-अलग पुरुष (Persons) के सर्वनाम एक साथ आएं, तो उनका क्रम निम्नलिखित नियमानुसार होता है:

  • A. Singular Pronouns in Good / Normal / Pleasant Contexts → Rule 231:
    Order: Second Person (You) → Third Person (He/She/They/Noun) → First Person (I).     A. एकवचन सर्वनाम (सामान्य/अच्छी बात में) → 231 का नियम:
    क्रम: You (2) → He/She/Mohan (3) → I (1).
    ✗ I and you will attend her wedding. → ✓ You and I will attend her wedding.
    ✓ You, Mohan and I will watch a movie tonight.
  • B. Plural Pronouns (In Any Context) → Rule 123:
    Order: First Person (We) → Second Person (You) → Third Person (They).     B. बहुवचन सर्वनाम (Plural) → 123 का नियम:
    क्रम: We (1) → You (2) → They (3).
    ✓ We, you and they are leaving for Mumbai tomorrow.
  • C. Confession of Guilt, Mistake, or Unpleasant Acts → Rule 123:
    When confessing a crime, blunder, or accepting punishment, good manners dictate taking the blame first!     C. भूल स्वीकार करने, अपराध या अप्रिय बात में → 123 का नियम:
    विनम्रता व शिष्टाचार के नाते अपनी गलती पहले स्वीकार की जाती है (I पहले):
    ✗ You and I will be punished. → ✓ I and you will be punished.
    ✓ I, you and he are responsible for this catastrophic loss.

Rule VII: Possessive Adjectives with Compound Subjectsनियम 7: संयुक्त कर्ताओं के साथ Possessive Adjective का प्रयोग

  • (A) Subjects joined by 'as well as, along with, together with, with, in addition to, like, unlike, rather than, except, but, no less than, nothing but':
    The possessive adjective must agree strictly with the FIRST subject!     (A) as well as, along with, together with आदि से जुड़े कर्ता:
    Possessive Adjective हमेशा पहले कर्ता (First Subject) के अनुसार आता है!
    ✗ Reena as well as her children has returned to their home. (Wrong)
    ✓ Reena as well as her children has returned to her home. (Correct)
    ✓ My sister along with her friends is doing her job at Delhi. (Correct)
  • (B) Subjects joined by 'either...or, neither...nor, not only...but also, none but':
    The possessive adjective must agree with the NEAREST subject!     (B) either...or, neither...nor, not only...but also से जुड़े कर्ता:
    Possessive Adjective हमेशा नजदीकी कर्ता (Nearest Subject) के अनुसार आता है!
    ✗ Neither the students nor the teacher was in their uniform. (Wrong)
    ✓ Neither the students nor the teacher was in his/her uniform. (Correct)
  • (C) When 'each, every, neither, either, anyone, everyone' is the subject:
    Possessive adjective must be Third Person Singular (his / her), NOT their!     (C) each, every, neither, either, everyone जब कर्ता हों:
    Possessive रूप हमेशा his/her (एकवचन) होगा, their नहीं!
    ✗ Everyone should do their duty. (Wrong)
    ✓ Everyone should do his duty. (Correct)
  • (D) When 'One' is the Subject → Use 'One's':
    If the indefinite pronoun 'one' is used as a subject, its possessive form must be one's (never his)!     (D) जब 'One' कर्ता हो → केवल 'one's' आएगा:
    'One' के साथ कभी भी his नहीं आता!
    ✗ One should do his duty sincerely. (Wrong)
    ✓ One should do one's duty sincerely. (Correct)
  • (E) Pronoun for different persons combined:
    1st + 2nd/3rd Person (You and I / He and I) → takes our.
    2nd + 3rd Person (You and he) → takes your.     (E) अलग-अलग पुरुष मिलकर:
    You and I → our (हमारा)
    You and he → your (तुम्हारा)
    ✓ You and I have brought our books.
    ✓ You and he have completed your work.

Rule VIII: Nouns That NEVER Take a Possessive Pronounनियम 8: जिन संज्ञाओं के पहले Possessive Case नहीं लगाया जाता

A possessive noun or pronoun should NOT be used directly with the following nouns: separation, leave, excuse, mention, report, pardon, sight, favour. निम्नलिखित 8 संज्ञाओं के ठीक पहले Possessive pronoun (your, his, my आदि) लगाना व्याकरण की दृष्टि से अशुद्ध है: separation, leave, excuse, mention, report, pardon, sight, favour.

Fixed Correct Idiomatic Patterns:

  • ✗ Your separation is very painful to me. (Wrong)
    ✓ Separation from you is very painful to me. (Correct)✓ तुम्हारी जुदाई मेरे लिए बहुत कष्टदायी है।
  • ✗ At his sight the robbers fled. (Wrong)
    ✓ At the sight of him the robbers fled. (Correct)✓ उसे देखते ही लुटेरे भाग गए।
  • ✗ I beg your favour, please. (Wrong)
    ✓ I beg a favour of/from you, please. (Correct)✓ कृपया मुझ पर यह उपकार/एहसान कीजिए।
  • ✗ She made your mention yesterday. (Wrong)
    ✓ She made mention of you yesterday. (Correct)✓ उसने कल तुम्हारा जिक्र किया।

Rule IX: 'Either / Neither' (For Two) vs 'Anyone / None' (For More Than Two)नियम 9: दो के लिए (Either/Neither) तथा दो से अधिक के लिए (Anyone/None)

  • For exactly TWO: Use Either (one of the two) and Neither (none of the two). केवल दो के लिए: Either (दोनों में से कोई एक) और Neither (दोनों में से कोई भी नहीं) का प्रयोग होता है।
    ✗ Anyone of his two eyes is defective. → ✓ Either of his two eyes is defective.
    ✗ None of his two arms was injured. → ✓ Neither of his two arms was injured.
  • For MORE THAN TWO: Use Anyone / Any and None. दो से अधिक (3 या अधिक) के लिए: Anyone/Any और None का प्रयोग होता है।
    ✗ Either of his four sons has sold the property. → ✓ Anyone of his four sons has sold the property.
    ✗ Neither of the ten candidates was selected. → ✓ None of the ten candidates was selected.

Rule X: Pronoun Rules in Question Tagsनियम 10: Question Tag में सर्वनाम के अचूक नियम

In a Question Tag, the subject pronoun and auxiliary verb must strictly correspond with the main clause: Question Tag में सर्वनाम और सहायक क्रिया हमेशा मुख्य वाक्य के अनुसार तय होते हैं:

  • 1. Positive Statement → Negative Tag: "She comes here daily, doesn't she?"
  • 2. Negative Statement → Positive Tag: "The boys are not going on picnic, are they?"
  • 3. Semi-Negative Adverbs (hardly, seldom, barely, scarcely, few, little):
    These words make the statement negative; hence the tag must be POSITIVE!     hardly, seldom, few, little जैसे शब्द नकारात्मक अर्थ देते हैं, अतः इनका Tag सकारात्मक (Positive) होगा:
    ✗ He is seldom absent, isn't he? → ✓ He is seldom absent, is he?
    ✗ Few students are working hard, aren't they? → ✓ Few students are working hard, are they?
  • 4. Indefinite Pronouns for Persons (everybody, someone, nobody, none, neither):
    Always take THEY as the subject pronoun in the question tag (and plural auxiliary verb)!     everybody, nobody, someone आदि के लिए Tag में सर्वनाम THEY और बहुवचन क्रिया आती है:
    ✓ Everybody can speak English, can't they?
    ✓ No one can speak English, can they?
    ✓ None of your friends like her, do they?
  • 5. Indefinite Pronouns for Things (everything, nothing, something):
    Always take IT in the tag:
    ✓ Everything is settled, isn't it?
    ✓ Nothing is settled, is it?
  • 6. Imperative Sentence Tags:
    "Don't close the room, will you?"
    "Let us play, shall we?" (Let us / Let's takes shall we)
    "Let them stay here, will you?" (Let him/them takes will you)

Rule XI: Use of 'Both' (Conjunction & Negative Restrictions)नियम 11: 'Both' का सही प्रयोग (and का साथ व नकारात्मक निषेध)

Both is followed strictly by and (never by as well as). Furthermore, Both is NEVER used in a negative sentence; use Neither instead! Both के साथ हमेशा and आता है (as well as कभी नहीं)। दूसरी महत्वपूर्ण बात: Both का प्रयोग नकारात्मक वाक्य में वर्जित है; नकारात्मक के लिए Neither का प्रयोग करें!

Examples:

  • ✗ Both you as well as my brother are going there. (Wrong)
    ✓ Both you and my brother are going there. (Correct)✓ तुम और मेरा भाई दोनों वहाँ जा रहे हैं।
  • ✗ Both of them are not going there. (Grave Grammatical Blunder!)
    ✓ Neither of them is going there. (Correct)✓ उनमें से कोई भी वहाँ नहीं जा रहा है।

Rule XII: 'Which' Instead of 'Who' for Choice / Selectionनियम 12: चुनाव या चयन (Choice) दर्शाने के लिए Who की जगह Which

Whenever you refer to a choice or selection between two or more persons or things, use Which instead of Who! जब दो या दो से अधिक व्यक्तियों या वस्तुओं में से किसी एक को चुनने (Choice/Selection) की बात हो, तो Who के स्थान पर Which का प्रयोग किया जाता है!

Examples:

  • ✗ Of the two sisters, who is the more intelligent? (Wrong)
    ✓ Of the two sisters, which is the more intelligent? (Correct)✓ दोनों बहनों में से कौन अधिक बुद्धिमान है?
  • ✗ Who is your father in the crowd? (Wrong)
    ✓ Which is your father in the crowd? (Correct)✓ भीड़ में तुम्हारे पिताश्री कौन-से हैं?

Rule XIII: No Noun After a Possessive Pronounनियम 13: Possessive Pronoun के बाद कभी Noun नहीं आता

Possessive Pronouns (mine, ours, yours, hers, theirs) replace both the possessive adjective and the noun. Hence, placing a noun after them is grammatically redundant. Possessive Pronouns (mine, ours, yours, hers, theirs) स्वयं संज्ञा का स्थान लेते हैं, इसलिए इनके बाद कभी संज्ञा (Noun) नहीं आती।

  • ✓ This book is mine. (= This is my book).
  • ✓ This shirt is yours. (= This is your shirt).
  • ✗ Our is a populous country. → ✓ Ours is a populous country.✓ हमारा देश घनी आबादी वाला देश है।

Rule XIV: 'Who' vs 'Whom' in Relative Clausesनियम 14: Relative Clause में Who और Whom का सही प्रयोग

Who functions as the Subject of the relative clause (does the action). Whom functions as the Object of the relative clause (receives the action).
🔥 TCS Hack / Shortcut: Temporarily strike out parenthetical interrupting clauses like "he said", "everybody knows", "I think" to instantly see whether the verb needs a subject or an object! Who: कर्ता (Subject) की जगह आता है जो क्रिया करता है। Whom: कर्म (Object) की जगह आता है।
🔥 शॉर्टकट ट्रिक: वाक्य के बीच में आने वाले "he said", "everybody knows" जैसे शब्दों को थोड़ी देर के लिए अनदेखा करें, तुरंत पता चल जाएगा कि क्रिया को कर्ता चाहिए (Who) या कर्म (Whom)।

Exam Practice Questions:

  • ✗ He was talking of the women who, he said, he met in America.
    (Analysis: Strike out 'he said'. We get 'he met [whom] in America'. Object is missing!)
    ✓ He was talking of the women whom, he said, he met in America.
  • ✗ She is the kind of lady whom, everybody knows, is intelligent.
    (Analysis: Strike out 'everybody knows'. We get '[who] is intelligent'. Subject for 'is' is missing!)
    ✓ She is the kind of lady who, everybody knows, is intelligent.

Rule XV: 'But' Used as a Relative Pronoun (= Who not / Which not)नियम 15: Relative Pronoun के रूप में 'But' (अर्थ: जो... न हो)

In classical literary and SSC exam English, But is often used after a negative principal clause as a relative pronoun equivalent to "who did not" or "which does not". नकारात्मक वाक्यों में But का प्रयोग Relative Pronoun की तरह होता है, जिसका अर्थ "जो... न हो" (who did not / which is not) होता है।

  • ✓ There was none but wept. (= There was no one who did not weep).✓ ऐसा कोई नहीं था जो रोया न हो।
  • ✓ There is no country but is corrupt. (= There is no country which is not corrupt).✓ ऐसा कोई देश नहीं जो भ्रष्ट न हो।

Rule XVI: Use of 'The Same' as a Pronoun Is Strictly Wrongनियम 16: Pronoun के रूप में 'The same' का प्रयोग पूर्णतः अशुद्ध है

In modern grammar, 'the same' must NEVER be used in place of personal pronouns like it or them. किसी वस्तु या संज्ञा के स्थान पर सर्वनाम के रूप में 'the same' लिखना गलत है; इसकी जगह it या them का प्रयोग करें।

  • ✗ I shall give you a book and the same is very useful. (Wrong)
    ✓ I shall give you a book and it is very useful. (Correct)✓ मैं तुम्हें एक किताब दूँगा और वह बहुत उपयोगी है।
  • ✗ He bought a house and is living in the same. (Wrong)
    ✓ He bought a house and is living in it. (Correct)✓ उसने एक घर खरीदा और वह उसी में रह रहा है।

Rule XVII: 'What' Is Used WITHOUT an Antecedentनियम 17: 'What' का प्रयोग बिना किसी पूर्ववर्ती संज्ञा (Antecedent) के होता है

What refers to things and means "that which" or "the thing which". It contains its own antecedent within itself. Therefore, you must NEVER place a noun antecedent before what! If a noun antecedent is present, use which or that. What का अर्थ होता है "वह जो"। इसमें पूर्ववर्ती संज्ञा पहले से समाहित होती है। अतः what के ठीक पहले कभी कोई संज्ञा (Noun) नहीं आ सकती! यदि पहले संज्ञा दी हो, तो which या that का प्रयोग करें।

Examples:

  • ✓ It is incredible what she said. (Correct — no noun before 'what').✓ उसने जो कहा, वह अविश्वसनीय है।
  • ✓ I don't believe in what you say. (Correct).✓ तुम जो कहते हो, मैं उस पर विश्वास नहीं करता।
  • ✗ I don't believe in the words what she uttered. (Wrong — 'words' is an antecedent noun!)
    ✓ I don't believe in the words that/which she uttered. (Correct).✓ मैं उन शब्दों पर विश्वास नहीं करता जो उसने कहे।

1. What is a Pronoun? (Definition & Purpose)

A Pronoun is a word used in place of a noun in order to avoid awkward and unnecessary repetition of the noun in a sentence or paragraph.

Example:

  • Awkward (Repeated Noun): Rahul bought a new car because Rahul loves driving, but Rahul's car broke down.
  • Natural & Correct (With Pronouns): Rahul bought a new car because he loves driving, but his car broke down.

Here, he and his replace the noun Rahul, making the sentence grammatically crisp and readable.

📌 Core Takeaway / मुख्य बिंदु:
A pronoun must always agree with the noun it replaces (its antecedent) in Person (1st, 2nd, 3rd), Number (Singular, Plural), and Gender (Masculine, Feminine, Neuter).

2. Classification: 8 Types of Pronouns

In standard English grammar tested in SSC CGL, CHSL, and CPO, Pronouns are classified into 8 core categories:

  1. Personal Pronouns: Refer to specific persons or things (I, we, you, he, she, it, they).
  2. Demonstrative Pronouns: Point out specific objects or position (this, that, these, those).
  3. Relative Pronouns: Connect dependent clauses and refer to a preceding noun (who, whom, whose, which, that).
  4. Interrogative Pronouns: Used to ask questions (who, whom, whose, what, which).
  5. Indefinite Pronouns: Refer to non-specific, vague persons or things (everybody, nobody, someone, all, few, none).
  6. Reflexive & Emphatic Pronouns: Turn the action back to the subject or emphasize it (myself, himself, themselves).
  7. Distributive Pronouns: Refer to persons or things one at a time (each, either, neither).
  8. Reciprocal Pronouns: Express mutual relationship (each other, one another).

3. Personal Pronouns & Master Case Table

Personal Pronouns change their form based on Person (1st, 2nd, 3rd) and Grammatical Case (Subjective, Objective, Possessive Adjective, and Possessive Pronoun). Understanding this table is fundamental to solving 90% of error-spotting questions in SSC.

Person (पुरुष) Number (वचन) Subjective (कर्ता रूप) Objective (कर्म रूप) Possessive Adjective (+ Noun) Possessive Pronoun (अकेला) Reflexive Pronoun
1st Person Singular (एकवचन) I (मैं) me (मुझे) my (मेरा + संज्ञा) mine (मेरा) myself (मैं स्वयं)
1st Person Plural (बहुवचन) we (हम) us (हमें) our (हमारा + संज्ञा) ours (हमारा) ourselves (हम स्वयं)
2nd Person Singular / Plural you (तुम/आप) you (तुम्हें) your (तुम्हारा + संज्ञा) yours (तुम्हारा) yourself / yourselves
3rd Person Singular (Male) he (वह - पुरुष) him (उसे) his (उसका + संज्ञा) his (उसका) himself (वह स्वयं)
3rd Person Singular (Female) she (वह - स्त्री) her (उसे) her (उसका + संज्ञा) hers (उसका) herself (वह स्वयं)
3rd Person Singular (Neuter) it (यह/वह - निर्जीव/जीव) it (इसे) its (इसका + संज्ञा) — (No pronoun form) itself (यह स्वयं)
3rd Person Plural they (वे) them (उन्हें) their (उनका + संज्ञा) theirs (उनका) themselves (वे स्वयं)

⚠️ Crucial Exam Distinction / महत्वपूर्ण परीक्षा अंतर:
Possessive Adjective always needs a noun immediately following it: "This is my car."
Possessive Pronoun stands completely alone without any noun: "This car is mine." (Never write mine car ✗).

4. Demonstrative, Relative, Distributive & Reciprocal Nuances

A. Demonstrative Pronoun vs Demonstrative Adjective:

  • Pronoun (Stands alone as subject): This is my house. / Those are ripe apples.
  • Adjective (Qualifies the noun next to it): This house is mine. / Those apples are ripe.

B. Relative Pronouns (Who, Whom, Which, That):

  • Who: Used strictly for persons as Subject ("The man who helped me is my friend.").
  • Whom: Used strictly for persons as Object ("The girl whom you met yesterday is my sister.").
  • Which: Used for non-living things, animals, or for choice ("The book which I bought is costly.").
  • That: Used for both persons and things, especially after superlatives, all, same, only, none.

C. Reciprocal Pronouns (Each other vs One another):

  • Each other: Strictly used for exactly TWO persons or things. ("Both brothers love each other.").
  • One another: Strictly used for MORE THAN TWO persons or things. ("The students helped one another.").

5. The 17 Golden Exam Rules of Pronoun (With Error-Spotting Examples)

Rule I: Verbs Followed by Reflexive Pronouns

When the subject of the verb is also the receiver of the action, the action is reflected. The following verbs are used reflexively if no direct object is present: acquit, absent, avail, reconcile, amuse, resign, avenge, revenge, enjoy, exert, apply, adapt, adjust, pride, overreach.

Examples (उदाहरण):

  • ✓ You should avail yourself of every opportunity in life.
  • ✗ They enjoyed during the summer vacation. (Incorrect)
    ✓ They enjoyed themselves during the summer vacation. (Correct)
  • ✓ He resigned himself to his failure.
  • ⚡ Crucial Note on 'Enjoy': If a direct object is already given, do NOT use a reflexive pronoun!
    "They enjoyed the movie last evening." (Here 'the movie' is the direct object, so themselves is not required).

Rule II: Verbs That Are NEVER Used Reflexively

The following intransitive/reflexive verbs do NOT take reflexive pronouns: keep, stop, turn, qualify, bathe, move, rest, hide.

Error-Spotting Practice Examples:

  • ✗ You should keep yourself away from bad companions. (Drop 'yourself')
    ✓ You should keep away from bad companions.
  • ✗ He has qualified himself for the post of Inspector. (Drop 'himself')
    ✓ He has qualified for the post of Inspector.
  • ✗ The thief hid himself behind the counter. (Drop 'himself')
    ✓ The thief hid behind the counter.

Rule III: Reflexive Pronouns Cannot Stand Alone as Subject or Object

A reflexive pronoun (myself, yourself, himself) cannot act as the subject or object of a verb unless it is preceded by the corresponding noun or pronoun. (Colloquial use of "Myself Rahul" in spoken English is 100% grammatically incorrect in exams!).

Exam Practice Questions:

  • ✗ Myself will see to it that you get justice. (Wrong)
    ✓ I will see to it that you get justice. (Correct)
  • ✗ Yourself and he reached the venue on time. (Wrong)
    ✓ You and he reached the venue on time. (Correct)
  • ✗ Raj will buy books for myself and my sister. (Wrong)
    ✓ Raj will buy books for me and my sister. (Correct)
  • ✓ I myself investigated the case. (Correct — here 'myself' is an Emphatic pronoun qualifying 'I').

Rule IV: Verb 'To Be' Takes Subjective Case Complement

When the complement of the verb 'to be' (is, am, are, was, were, been) is a personal pronoun, it must always be in the Subjective (Nominative) case, NOT the objective case.

Exam Examples:

  • ✗ It is me who have brought you home. (Wrong)
    ✓ It is I who have brought you home. (Correct)
  • ✗ Was it her who did it for you? (Wrong)
    ✓ Was it she who did it for you? (Correct)
  • ✗ If I were him, I would not accept the bribe. (Wrong)
    ✓ If I were he, I would not accept the bribe. (Correct)

Rule V: Verbs and Prepositions Are Followed by Objective Case

Whenever a pronoun follows a transitive verb or a preposition (such as between, to, for, with, except, like, let), it must always be in the Objective Case (me, him, her, us, them).

Exam Traps:

  • ✗ Between you and I, Suhani is very intelligent. (Wrong)
    ✓ Between you and me, Suhani is very intelligent. (Correct)
  • ✗ Let they go there immediately. (Wrong)
    ✓ Let them go there immediately. (Correct)
  • ✗ She is teaching Rohit and she. (Wrong)
    ✓ She is teaching Rohit and her. (Correct)
  • ✗ Everyone attended the party except he. (Wrong)
    ✓ Everyone attended the party except him. (Correct)

Rule VI: Order of Pronouns (231 vs 123 Rules)

When pronouns of different persons are used together in a single sentence, their sequence is strictly governed by etiquette and context:

  • A. Singular Pronouns in Good / Normal / Pleasant Contexts → Rule 231:
    Order: Second Person (You) → Third Person (He/She/They/Noun) → First Person (I).
    ✗ I and you will attend her wedding. → ✓ You and I will attend her wedding.
    ✓ You, Mohan and I will watch a movie tonight.
  • B. Plural Pronouns (In Any Context) → Rule 123:
    Order: First Person (We) → Second Person (You) → Third Person (They).
    ✓ We, you and they are leaving for Mumbai tomorrow.
  • C. Confession of Guilt, Mistake, or Unpleasant Acts → Rule 123:
    When confessing a crime, blunder, or accepting punishment, good manners dictate taking the blame first!
    ✗ You and I will be punished. → ✓ I and you will be punished.
    ✓ I, you and he are responsible for this catastrophic loss.

Rule VII: Possessive Adjectives with Compound Subjects

  • (A) Subjects joined by 'as well as, along with, together with, with, in addition to, like, unlike, rather than, except, but, no less than, nothing but':
    The possessive adjective must agree strictly with the FIRST subject!
    ✗ Reena as well as her children has returned to their home. (Wrong)
    ✓ Reena as well as her children has returned to her home. (Correct)
    ✓ My sister along with her friends is doing her job at Delhi. (Correct)
  • (B) Subjects joined by 'either...or, neither...nor, not only...but also, none but':
    The possessive adjective must agree with the NEAREST subject!
    ✗ Neither the students nor the teacher was in their uniform. (Wrong)
    ✓ Neither the students nor the teacher was in his/her uniform. (Correct)
  • (C) When 'each, every, neither, either, anyone, everyone' is the subject:
    Possessive adjective must be Third Person Singular (his / her), NOT their!
    ✗ Everyone should do their duty. (Wrong)
    ✓ Everyone should do his duty. (Correct)
  • (D) When 'One' is the Subject → Use 'One's':
    If the indefinite pronoun 'one' is used as a subject, its possessive form must be one's (never his)!
    ✗ One should do his duty sincerely. (Wrong)
    ✓ One should do one's duty sincerely. (Correct)
  • (E) Pronoun for different persons combined:
    1st + 2nd/3rd Person (You and I / He and I) → takes our.
    2nd + 3rd Person (You and he) → takes your.
    ✓ You and I have brought our books.
    ✓ You and he have completed your work.

Rule VIII: Nouns That NEVER Take a Possessive Pronoun

A possessive noun or pronoun should NOT be used directly with the following nouns: separation, leave, excuse, mention, report, pardon, sight, favour.

Fixed Correct Idiomatic Patterns:

  • ✗ Your separation is very painful to me. (Wrong)
    ✓ Separation from you is very painful to me. (Correct)
  • ✗ At his sight the robbers fled. (Wrong)
    ✓ At the sight of him the robbers fled. (Correct)
  • ✗ I beg your favour, please. (Wrong)
    ✓ I beg a favour of/from you, please. (Correct)
  • ✗ She made your mention yesterday. (Wrong)
    ✓ She made mention of you yesterday. (Correct)

Rule IX: 'Either / Neither' (For Two) vs 'Anyone / None' (For More Than Two)

  • For exactly TWO: Use Either (one of the two) and Neither (none of the two).
    ✗ Anyone of his two eyes is defective. → ✓ Either of his two eyes is defective.
    ✗ None of his two arms was injured. → ✓ Neither of his two arms was injured.
  • For MORE THAN TWO: Use Anyone / Any and None.
    ✗ Either of his four sons has sold the property. → ✓ Anyone of his four sons has sold the property.
    ✗ Neither of the ten candidates was selected. → ✓ None of the ten candidates was selected.

Rule X: Pronoun Rules in Question Tags

In a Question Tag, the subject pronoun and auxiliary verb must strictly correspond with the main clause:

  • 1. Positive Statement → Negative Tag: "She comes here daily, doesn't she?"
  • 2. Negative Statement → Positive Tag: "The boys are not going on picnic, are they?"
  • 3. Semi-Negative Adverbs (hardly, seldom, barely, scarcely, few, little):
    These words make the statement negative; hence the tag must be POSITIVE!
    ✗ He is seldom absent, isn't he? → ✓ He is seldom absent, is he?
    ✗ Few students are working hard, aren't they? → ✓ Few students are working hard, are they?
  • 4. Indefinite Pronouns for Persons (everybody, someone, nobody, none, neither):
    Always take THEY as the subject pronoun in the question tag (and plural auxiliary verb)!
    ✓ Everybody can speak English, can't they?
    ✓ No one can speak English, can they?
    ✓ None of your friends like her, do they?
  • 5. Indefinite Pronouns for Things (everything, nothing, something):
    Always take IT in the tag:
    ✓ Everything is settled, isn't it?
    ✓ Nothing is settled, is it?
  • 6. Imperative Sentence Tags:
    "Don't close the room, will you?"
    "Let us play, shall we?" (Let us / Let's takes shall we)
    "Let them stay here, will you?" (Let him/them takes will you)

Rule XI: Use of 'Both' (Conjunction & Negative Restrictions)

Both is followed strictly by and (never by as well as). Furthermore, Both is NEVER used in a negative sentence; use Neither instead!

Examples:

  • ✗ Both you as well as my brother are going there. (Wrong)
    ✓ Both you and my brother are going there. (Correct)
  • ✗ Both of them are not going there. (Grave Grammatical Blunder!)
    ✓ Neither of them is going there. (Correct)

Rule XII: 'Which' Instead of 'Who' for Choice / Selection

Whenever you refer to a choice or selection between two or more persons or things, use Which instead of Who!

Examples:

  • ✗ Of the two sisters, who is the more intelligent? (Wrong)
    ✓ Of the two sisters, which is the more intelligent? (Correct)
  • ✗ Who is your father in the crowd? (Wrong)
    ✓ Which is your father in the crowd? (Correct)

Rule XIII: No Noun After a Possessive Pronoun

Possessive Pronouns (mine, ours, yours, hers, theirs) replace both the possessive adjective and the noun. Hence, placing a noun after them is grammatically redundant.

  • ✓ This book is mine. (= This is my book).
  • ✓ This shirt is yours. (= This is your shirt).
  • ✗ Our is a populous country. → ✓ Ours is a populous country.

Rule XIV: 'Who' vs 'Whom' in Relative Clauses

Who functions as the Subject of the relative clause (does the action). Whom functions as the Object of the relative clause (receives the action).
🔥 TCS Hack / Shortcut: Temporarily strike out parenthetical interrupting clauses like "he said", "everybody knows", "I think" to instantly see whether the verb needs a subject or an object!

Exam Practice Questions:

  • ✗ He was talking of the women who, he said, he met in America.
    (Analysis: Strike out 'he said'. We get 'he met [whom] in America'. Object is missing!)
    ✓ He was talking of the women whom, he said, he met in America.
  • ✗ She is the kind of lady whom, everybody knows, is intelligent.
    (Analysis: Strike out 'everybody knows'. We get '[who] is intelligent'. Subject for 'is' is missing!)
    ✓ She is the kind of lady who, everybody knows, is intelligent.

Rule XV: 'But' Used as a Relative Pronoun (= Who not / Which not)

In classical literary and SSC exam English, But is often used after a negative principal clause as a relative pronoun equivalent to "who did not" or "which does not".

  • ✓ There was none but wept. (= There was no one who did not weep).
  • ✓ There is no country but is corrupt. (= There is no country which is not corrupt).

Rule XVI: Use of 'The Same' as a Pronoun Is Strictly Wrong

In modern grammar, 'the same' must NEVER be used in place of personal pronouns like it or them.

  • ✗ I shall give you a book and the same is very useful. (Wrong)
    ✓ I shall give you a book and it is very useful. (Correct)
  • ✗ He bought a house and is living in the same. (Wrong)
    ✓ He bought a house and is living in it. (Correct)

Rule XVII: 'What' Is Used WITHOUT an Antecedent

What refers to things and means "that which" or "the thing which". It contains its own antecedent within itself. Therefore, you must NEVER place a noun antecedent before what! If a noun antecedent is present, use which or that.

Examples:

  • ✓ It is incredible what she said. (Correct — no noun before 'what').
  • ✓ I don't believe in what you say. (Correct).
  • ✗ I don't believe in the words what she uttered. (Wrong — 'words' is an antecedent noun!)
    ✓ I don't believe in the words that/which she uttered. (Correct).

6. Quick Revision: Top 8 Pronoun Traps

Exam Trap (नियम) Incorrect (अशुद्ध रूप) Correct (शुद्ध रूप)
Verbs with Reflexive He absented from the meeting. He absented himself from the meeting.
Verbs without Reflexive He hid himself in the closet. He hid in the closet.
Order of Pronouns (Normal) I, you and he will go. You, he and I will go (231 rule).

One as Subject One must respect his parents. One must respect one's parents.
Choice between Persons Who of the two sisters is taller? Which of the two sisters is taller?
Negative with Both Both of them did not come. Neither of them came.
Antecedent with What The advice what he gave was good. The advice that/which he gave was good.

Exam Practice Questions:


  • ✓ मैं देखूंगा कि तुम्हें न्याय मिले।

  • ✓ तुम और वह समय पर कार्यक्रम स्थल पर पहुंचे।

  • ✓ राज मेरे और मेरी बहन के लिए किताबें खरीदेगा।

नियम 4: 'To Be' क्रिया (is/am/are/was/were) के बाद Subjective रूप आता है

जब 'To Be' क्रिया (is, am, are, was, were) का पूरक कोई सर्वनाम हो, तो वह हमेशा Subjective Case (I, he, she, we, they) में आएगा, Objective (me, him, her, us, them) में नहीं।

Exam Examples:


  • ✓ मैं ही हूँ जो तुम्हें घर लेकर आया हूँ।

  • ✓ क्या वह वही थी जिसने तुम्हारे लिए यह किया?

  • ✓ यदि मैं उसकी जगह होता, तो रिश्वत न लेता।

नियम 5: क्रिया तथा Preposition के बाद हमेशा Objective Case आता है

किसी भी क्रिया अथवा Preposition (जैसे between, to, for, with, except, let, but) के बाद आने वाला सर्वनाम हमेशा Objective Case (me, him, her, us, them) में होना चाहिए।

Exam Traps:


  • ✓ तुम्हारे और मेरे बीच की बात है, सुहानी बहुत बुद्धिमान है।

  • ✓ उन्हें तुरंत वहाँ जाने दो।

  • ✓ वह रोहित और उसे पढ़ा रही है।

  • ✓ उसके अलावा सभी पार्टी में शामिल हुए।

नियम 6: सर्वनामों का क्रम (231 और 123 का नियम)

जब एक ही वाक्य में अलग-अलग पुरुष (Persons) के सर्वनाम एक साथ आएं, तो उनका क्रम निम्नलिखित नियमानुसार होता है:

  • A. एकवचन सर्वनाम (सामान्य/अच्छी बात में) → 231 का नियम:
    क्रम: You (2) → He/She/Mohan (3) → I (1).
    ✗ I and you will attend her wedding. → ✓ You and I will attend her wedding.
    ✓ You, Mohan and I will watch a movie tonight.
  • B. बहुवचन सर्वनाम (Plural) → 123 का नियम:
    क्रम: We (1) → You (2) → They (3).
    ✓ We, you and they are leaving for Mumbai tomorrow.
  • C. भूल स्वीकार करने, अपराध या अप्रिय बात में → 123 का नियम:
    विनम्रता व शिष्टाचार के नाते अपनी गलती पहले स्वीकार की जाती है (I पहले):
    ✗ You and I will be punished. → ✓ I and you will be punished.
    ✓ I, you and he are responsible for this catastrophic loss.

नियम 7: संयुक्त कर्ताओं के साथ Possessive Adjective का प्रयोग

  • (A) as well as, along with, together with आदि से जुड़े कर्ता:
    Possessive Adjective हमेशा पहले कर्ता (First Subject) के अनुसार आता है!
    ✗ Reena as well as her children has returned to their home. (Wrong)
    ✓ Reena as well as her children has returned to her home. (Correct)
    ✓ My sister along with her friends is doing her job at Delhi. (Correct)
  • (B) either...or, neither...nor, not only...but also से जुड़े कर्ता:
    Possessive Adjective हमेशा नजदीकी कर्ता (Nearest Subject) के अनुसार आता है!
    ✗ Neither the students nor the teacher was in their uniform. (Wrong)
    ✓ Neither the students nor the teacher was in his/her uniform. (Correct)
  • (C) each, every, neither, either, everyone जब कर्ता हों:
    Possessive रूप हमेशा his/her (एकवचन) होगा, their नहीं!
    ✗ Everyone should do their duty. (Wrong)
    ✓ Everyone should do his duty. (Correct)
  • (D) जब 'One' कर्ता हो → केवल 'one's' आएगा:
    'One' के साथ कभी भी his नहीं आता!
    ✗ One should do his duty sincerely. (Wrong)
    ✓ One should do one's duty sincerely. (Correct)
  • (E) अलग-अलग पुरुष मिलकर:
    You and I → our (हमारा)
    You and he → your (तुम्हारा)
    ✓ You and I have brought our books.
    ✓ You and he have completed your work.

नियम 8: जिन संज्ञाओं के पहले Possessive Case नहीं लगाया जाता

निम्नलिखित 8 संज्ञाओं के ठीक पहले Possessive pronoun (your, his, my आदि) लगाना व्याकरण की दृष्टि से अशुद्ध है: separation, leave, excuse, mention, report, pardon, sight, favour.

Fixed Correct Idiomatic Patterns:


  • ✓ तुम्हारी जुदाई मेरे लिए बहुत कष्टदायी है।

  • ✓ उसे देखते ही लुटेरे भाग गए।

  • ✓ कृपया मुझ पर यह उपकार/एहसान कीजिए।

  • ✓ उसने कल तुम्हारा जिक्र किया।

नियम 9: दो के लिए (Either/Neither) तथा दो से अधिक के लिए (Anyone/None)

  • केवल दो के लिए: Either (दोनों में से कोई एक) और Neither (दोनों में से कोई भी नहीं) का प्रयोग होता है।
    ✗ Anyone of his two eyes is defective. → ✓ Either of his two eyes is defective.
    ✗ None of his two arms was injured. → ✓ Neither of his two arms was injured.
  • दो से अधिक (3 या अधिक) के लिए: Anyone/Any और None का प्रयोग होता है।
    ✗ Either of his four sons has sold the property. → ✓ Anyone of his four sons has sold the property.
    ✗ Neither of the ten candidates was selected. → ✓ None of the ten candidates was selected.

नियम 10: Question Tag में सर्वनाम के अचूक नियम

Question Tag में सर्वनाम और सहायक क्रिया हमेशा मुख्य वाक्य के अनुसार तय होते हैं:

  • hardly, seldom, few, little जैसे शब्द नकारात्मक अर्थ देते हैं, अतः इनका Tag सकारात्मक (Positive) होगा:
    ✗ He is seldom absent, isn't he? → ✓ He is seldom absent, is he?
    ✗ Few students are working hard, aren't they? → ✓ Few students are working hard, are they?
  • everybody, nobody, someone आदि के लिए Tag में सर्वनाम THEY और बहुवचन क्रिया आती है:
    ✓ Everybody can speak English, can't they?
    ✓ No one can speak English, can they?
    ✓ None of your friends like her, do they?

  • ✓ Everything is settled, isn't it?
    ✓ Nothing is settled, is it?

नियम 11: 'Both' का सही प्रयोग (and का साथ व नकारात्मक निषेध)

Both के साथ हमेशा and आता है (as well as कभी नहीं)। दूसरी महत्वपूर्ण बात: Both का प्रयोग नकारात्मक वाक्य में वर्जित है; नकारात्मक के लिए Neither का प्रयोग करें!

Examples:


  • ✓ तुम और मेरा भाई दोनों वहाँ जा रहे हैं।

  • ✓ उनमें से कोई भी वहाँ नहीं जा रहा है।

नियम 12: चुनाव या चयन (Choice) दर्शाने के लिए Who की जगह Which

जब दो या दो से अधिक व्यक्तियों या वस्तुओं में से किसी एक को चुनने (Choice/Selection) की बात हो, तो Who के स्थान पर Which का प्रयोग किया जाता है!

Examples:


  • ✓ दोनों बहनों में से कौन अधिक बुद्धिमान है?

  • ✓ भीड़ में तुम्हारे पिताश्री कौन-से हैं?

नियम 13: Possessive Pronoun के बाद कभी Noun नहीं आता

Possessive Pronouns (mine, ours, yours, hers, theirs) स्वयं संज्ञा का स्थान लेते हैं, इसलिए इनके बाद कभी संज्ञा (Noun) नहीं आती।

  • ✓ हमारा देश घनी आबादी वाला देश है।

नियम 14: Relative Clause में Who और Whom का सही प्रयोग

Who: कर्ता (Subject) की जगह आता है जो क्रिया करता है। Whom: कर्म (Object) की जगह आता है।
🔥 शॉर्टकट ट्रिक: वाक्य के बीच में आने वाले "he said", "everybody knows" जैसे शब्दों को थोड़ी देर के लिए अनदेखा करें, तुरंत पता चल जाएगा कि क्रिया को कर्ता चाहिए (Who) या कर्म (Whom)।

Exam Practice Questions:

नियम 15: Relative Pronoun के रूप में 'But' (अर्थ: जो... न हो)

नकारात्मक वाक्यों में But का प्रयोग Relative Pronoun की तरह होता है, जिसका अर्थ "जो... न हो" (who did not / which is not) होता है।

  • ✓ ऐसा कोई नहीं था जो रोया न हो।
  • ✓ ऐसा कोई देश नहीं जो भ्रष्ट न हो।

नियम 16: Pronoun के रूप में 'The same' का प्रयोग पूर्णतः अशुद्ध है

किसी वस्तु या संज्ञा के स्थान पर सर्वनाम के रूप में 'the same' लिखना गलत है; इसकी जगह it या them का प्रयोग करें।


  • ✓ मैं तुम्हें एक किताब दूँगा और वह बहुत उपयोगी है।

  • ✓ उसने एक घर खरीदा और वह उसी में रह रहा है।

नियम 17: 'What' का प्रयोग बिना किसी पूर्ववर्ती संज्ञा (Antecedent) के होता है

What का अर्थ होता है "वह जो"। इसमें पूर्ववर्ती संज्ञा पहले से समाहित होती है। अतः what के ठीक पहले कभी कोई संज्ञा (Noun) नहीं आ सकती! यदि पहले संज्ञा दी हो, तो which या that का प्रयोग करें।

Examples:

  • ✓ उसने जो कहा, वह अविश्वसनीय है।
  • ✓ तुम जो कहते हो, मैं उस पर विश्वास नहीं करता।

  • ✓ मैं उन शब्दों पर विश्वास नहीं करता जो उसने कहे।

1. What is a Tense? (Time vs State of Action)1. काल (Tense) क्या है? (समय एवं कार्य की अवस्था)

A Tense is defined as that form of a verb which indicates two fundamental dimensions:

  1. The Time of an Action: When the action takes place (Present, Past, or Future).
  2. The State / Aspect of an Action: How the action exists (habitual, in progress, fully completed, or continuing over a period of time).

(A) Time of an Action:

  • Present: He goes to school. (Action relates to present time).
  • Past: He went to school. (Action relates to past time).
  • Future: He will go to school. (Action relates to future time).

(B) State / Function of an Action:

  • Habitual (Indefinite): I write letters regularly. (General habit).
  • Progressive (Continuous): I am writing a letter. (Ongoing action right now).
  • Preceding (Perfect): I have just written a letter. (Completed before now, connected to present).
  • Time Expression (Perfect Continuous): I have been writing a letter for two hours. (Began in past, still continuing).

काल (Tense) क्रिया का वह रूप है जो केवल समय (Time) ही नहीं बताता, बल्कि कार्य की अवस्था (State of Action) भी दर्शाता है:

  1. काम का समय (Time): कार्य कब हुआ — वर्तमान (Present), भूतकाल (Past), या भविष्य (Future)।
  2. काम की अवस्था (State/Aspect): कार्य किस हाल में है — नियमित आदत (Habitual), चालू है (Progressive), पूरा हो चुका है (Preceding/Perfect), या किसी समय से जारी है (Time Expression)।

प्रत्येक मुख्य काल (Present, Past, Future) के चार रूप होते हैं, जिससे अंग्रेजी व्याकरण में कुल 12 Tenses बनते हैं।

⏱️ The 3 Time Frames / समय के तीन ढाँचे:
1. Point of Time: A specific exact moment (e.g., in 1947, on Monday, at 7:00 PM).
2. Period of Time: A duration without fixed start point (e.g., for ten years, from Monday to Saturday).
3. Expression of Time: Combination of point and duration (e.g., winter 1950, since childhood). 1. निश्चित बिंदु-समय (Point of Time): एक निश्चित समय बिंदु (जैसे: 1947 में, सोमवार को, सुबह 7 बजे)।
2. अवधि (Period of Time): समय का अंतराल (जैसे: 10 वर्षों के लिए, दो घंटे से)।
3. बिंदु + अवधि (Expression of Time): जैसे: 1947 की सर्दी, बचपन से।

2. The Present Indefinite Tense (Simple Present)2. सामान्य वर्तमान काल (Present Indefinite Tense)

Basic Sentence Structure:

  • Affirmative: Subject + V1 (s/es with 3rd person singular) + Object
  • Negative: Subject + do/does not + V1 + Object
  • Interrogative: Do/Does + Subject + V1 + Object?

Core Usages:

  1. Habits, Customs, Routines & Repeated Actions: Expressed with Adverbs of Frequency: often, seldom, usually, never, occasionally, sometimes, normally, generally, always, frequently, rarely, daily.
    Example: "The old lady goes for a walk in the morning daily." / "Suhani always comes in time."
  2. Permanent Nature & Eternal Scientific Principles (Universal Truths):
    Example: "Water boils at 100°C." / "Rivers freeze at high altitude." / "Plants prepare their own food."
  3. Historical Present (Dramatic Narration): Used by commentators and storytellers to make past events vivid.
    Example: "Now Netaji enters and addresses the Indian soldiers."
  4. Fixed Future Arrangement / Timetable: Official schedules and planned future events.
    Example: "The Prime Minister arrives from New York tomorrow." / "He leaves for his new job next week."

संरचना (Structure):

  • सकारात्मक: Subject + V1 (एकवचन कर्ता के साथ s/es) + Object (He writes / They write)
  • नकारात्मक: Subject + do/does not + V1 + Object (He does not write)

प्रमुख उपयोग:

  1. आदत, दिनचर्या व बार-बार होने वाले काम: इसके साथ Adverbs of Frequency आते हैं: often (अक्सर), seldom (शायद ही कभी), usually (आमतौर पर), never (कभी नहीं), always (हमेशा), daily (रोज़) आदि।
  2. सार्वभौमिक एवं वैज्ञानिक सत्य (Universal Truths): जो बातें हमेशा सच रहती हैं, वे सदा Present Indefinite में लिखी जाती हैं: "Water boils at 100°C." (पानी 100°C पर उबलता है)।
  3. ऐतिहासिक वर्तमान (Historical Present): बीती घटना को आँखों के सामने जीवंत सुनाने हेतु: "Now, Arjun shoots arrows at Bhishma."
  4. निश्चित भविष्य की समय-सारणी (Future Arrangement): पक्के कार्यक्रम वाले भविष्य के कार्य हेतु: "The train leaves at 5:00 PM tomorrow."

3. Present Continuous Tense & The Stative Verbs Master List3. चालू वर्तमान काल एवं Stative Verbs (जो क्रियाएँ -ing में नहीं आतीं)

Structure: Subject + is/am/are + V-ing + Object

Primary Functions:

  • Action in Progress: Action happening at the moment of speaking (temporary nature): "It is raining outside." / "She is swimming in the river."
  • Near Future Definite Plan: "I am going to the cinema tomorrow." / "She is coming next week."
  • With 'Always' (Expressing Irritation / Complaint): When always is used with continuous tense, it indicates annoying behavior: "She is always nagging her children." / "He is always praising his friends."

🔥 Stative Verbs (Non-Progressive Verbs):
Certain verbs describe a state, condition, perception, or feeling rather than a dynamic physical activity. These verbs CANNOT be used in continuous (-ing) tenses under normal circumstances!

संरचना: Subject + is/am/are + V-ing + Object

प्रमुख उपयोग:

  • बोलते समय जारी कार्य: "It is raining outside." (बाहर बारिश हो रही है)।
  • निकट भविष्य की पक्की योजना: "I am meeting the doctor tomorrow."
  • 'always' के साथ शिकायत या नाराजगी का भाव: "He is always praising his friends." (वह हमेशा अपने दोस्तों की तारीफ ही करता रहता है)।

🔥 Stative Verbs का सबसे बड़ा नियम:
जो क्रियाएं कोई शारीरिक काम नहीं, बल्कि अवस्था (State), इंद्रिय-बोध (Perception), स्वामित्व (Possession) या मानसिक भाव दर्शाती हैं, उनका Continuous (-ing) रूप नहीं बनता! इन्हें सदा Simple Present में लिखा जाता है।

4. Feelings & Emotions (भाव / मनोदशा) love, hate, like, want, wish, desire, believe I am not hating him. ✗ I don't hate him. ✓
5. Verbs in General (सामान्य अवस्था) look, seem, appear, resemble, cost, require, stand The book is containing good content. ✗ The book contains good content. ✓

Some verbs can be used in the -ing form ONLY when their meaning shifts from a state to an active physical action: कुछ क्रियाएं -ing में तभी आ सकती हैं जब उनका अर्थ 'अवस्था' से बदलकर 'सक्रिय कार्य' हो जाए:

  • Smell (State): The rose smells sweet. (गुलाब की खुशबू मीठी है — Stative)
    Smell (Active Action): She is smelling a black rose. (वह काला गुलाब सूँघ रही है — Progressive)
  • Have (Possession): She has a large house. (उसके पास बड़ा घर है — Stative)

4. Present Perfect Tense & The 2 Cardinal Rules4. पूर्ण वर्तमान काल (Present Perfect) एवं 2 अचूक नियम

Structure: Subject + has/have + V3 + Object

The Present Perfect Tense represents an action completed in the past that has a direct, active link with the present moment.

Common Signal Adverbs: ever, just, already, recently, lately, yet, so far, till now, by the time.

  • "I have just finished my breakfast." (अभी-अभी खाया है).
  • "We have seen this movie already." (पहले ही देख चुके हैं).
  • "We haven't seen Reeta lately." (इधर हाल में नहीं देखा).

संरचना: Subject + has/have + V3 + Object

यह काल भूतकाल और वर्तमान का संगम है — कार्य भले ही अतीत में पूरा हुआ हो, लेकिन उसका प्रभाव या संबंध वर्तमान से जुड़ा रहता है।

पहचान वाले शब्द: just (अभी-अभी), already (पहले ही), recently/lately (हाल ही में), yet/so far (अब तक - नकारात्मक वाक्यों में)।

Golden Rule 1: Present Perfect + Definite Past Point of Time = SIMPLE PASTस्वर्णिम नियम 1: Present Perfect + निश्चित बीता समय = SIMPLE PAST

If a sentence contains a definite finished point of time in the past (such as yesterday, two days ago, last year, in 1947, the other day, formerly), you MUST use Simple Past (V2), NEVER Present Perfect (has/have + V3)! यदि वाक्य में बीते हुए समय का कोई निश्चित शब्द (जैसे yesterday, ago, last week, in 2020, the other day) दिया हो, तो वहाँ कभी भी Present Perfect (has/have + V3) नहीं आता, बल्कि हमेशा Simple Past (V2) आता है!

Top Recurring SSC Questions:

  • ✗ She has returned two days ago. (Incorrect — omit 'has')
    ✓ She returned two days ago. (Correct — Simple Past)✓ वह दो दिन पहले लौटी।
  • ✗ I have met your brother yesterday. (Incorrect — omit 'have')
    ✓ I met your brother yesterday. (Correct)✓ मैं कल तुम्हारे भाई से मिला।
  • ✗ India has won independence in 1947. (Incorrect)
    ✓ India won independence in 1947. (Correct)

Golden Rule 2: Present Indefinite + Time Expression = PRESENT PERFECTस्वर्णिम नियम 2: वर्तमान क्रिया + अवधि/बिंदु-समय (Since/For) = PRESENT PERFECT

When a state or action started in the past and continues into the present with since, for, how long, whole, all along, you cannot use Simple Present; you MUST use Present Perfect! यदि कोई स्थिति अतीत से शुरू होकर अब तक बनी हुई है और साथ में since / for / how long लगा है, तो वहाँ Simple Present नहीं, बल्कि Present Perfect आएगा:

  • ✗ He knows me for two years. (Wrong)
    ✓ He has known me for two years. (Correct)✓ वह मुझे दो साल से जानता है।
  • ✗ She owns this parlour since 2002. (Wrong)
    ✓ She has owned this parlour since 2002. (Correct)✓ वह 2002 से इस पार्लर की मालकिन है।

5. Past Tenses & Past Perfect (The 'Past of the Past' Rule)5. भूतकाल एवं Past Perfect ('भूतकाल का भूतकाल' नियम)

A. Past Indefinite (Simple Past): Subject + V2 + Object

  • Used for completed past actions with past time markers: "She bought a car two years ago."
  • Used for past habits: "He always carried an umbrella." / "I used to go to Delhi by train."

B. Past Continuous: Subject + was/were + V-ing + Object

  • Action in progress in the past: "It was still raining when I reached there."

C. Past Perfect (had + V3):

Past Perfect does NOT simply mean past; it means the earlier of two past actions!

A. Past Indefinite (Simple Past): Subject + V2 + Object
बीते समय में पूरा हुआ एकल कार्य या पुरानी आदतें (used to / would): "I met him yesterday."

B. Past Perfect (had + V3) — परीक्षा का सबसे महत्वपूर्ण नियम:

जब भूतकाल में दो कार्य हुए हों, तो जो कार्य पहले पूरा हुआ, उसे Past Perfect (had + V3) में लिखा जाता है, और जो कार्य बाद में हुआ, उसे Simple Past (V2) में लिखा जाता है!

The Two Past Actions Formula (Before / After)दो बीते कार्यों का अचूक सूत्र (Before / After)

1st Action (Earlier) → Past Perfect [had + V3]
2nd Action (Later) → Simple Past [V2]
  • ✓ The patient had died before the doctor arrived.✓ डॉक्टर के आने से पहले मरीज मर चुका था। (मरीज पहले मरा = had died; डॉक्टर बाद में आया = arrived)।
  • ✓ The train had left before we reached the station.✓ हमारे स्टेशन पहुँचने से पहले ट्रेन जा चुकी थी।
  • ✓ I finished the book after I had returned from college.✓ कॉलेज से लौटने के बाद मैंने किताब खत्म की।
  • ⚡ Single Action Blunder: Never use Past Perfect for a single standalone past action without an earlier reference point!
    ✗ I had gone to Delhi last week. (Incorrect)
    ✓ I went to Delhi last week. (Correct — Simple Past)

When verbs like want, hope, expect, think, suppose, intend are used with had + V3, it indicates that the action was desired or planned, but DID NOT take place! जब want, hope, expect, intend जैसी क्रियाओं के साथ had + V3 का प्रयोग होता है, तो इसका अर्थ होता है कि वह इच्छा या योजना पूरी नहीं हो सकी:

  • ✓ I had wanted to help my brother. (Meaning: but I could not help).✓ मैं अपने भाई की मदद करना चाहता था (पर कर न सका)।
  • ✓ I had expected to pass the exam. (Meaning: but I did not pass).✓ मुझे परीक्षा पास करने की उम्मीद थी (पर पास न हुआ)।
  • ✓ Vishal had intended to set up his own business. (Meaning: but could not).✓ विशाल का अपना व्यवसाय शुरू करने का इरादा था (पर न कर सका)।

6. Future Tenses & The Nuance of Shall vs Will6. भविष्यत् काल एवं Shall बनाम Will का अचूक नियम

Structure:

  • Future Indefinite: Subject + will/shall + V1 (They will come here shortly).
  • Future Continuous: Subject + will/shall be + V-ing (She will be waiting for me when I reach).
  • Future Perfect: Subject + will/shall have + V3 (She will have prepared food before I reach home).

The Shall vs Will Rule (Normal vs Emphatic/Modal):

  • Ordinary / Neutral Future: Use Shall with 1st Person (I, We); Use Will with 2nd & 3rd Person (You, He, She, They).
  • Determination, Promise, Threat, Order, or Official Duty: The rule is REVERSED!
    • Use Will with I, We (e.g., "I will help my brother." — Firm determination).
    • Use Shall with You, He, They (e.g., "You shall not move." — Strict order; "They shall be rewarded." — Solemn promise).

Shall बनाम Will का नियम:

  • साधारण भविष्य (General Future): I / We के साथ shall; You / He / She / They के साथ will आता है।
    "I shall go to Delhi." (मैं दिल्ली जाऊँगा — जा भी सकता हूँ, नहीं भी)।
  • आदेश, वादा, दृढ़ निश्चय, कर्तव्य या धमकी (Determination/Order/Promise): नियम उल्टा हो जाता है!
    1st Person (I, We) के साथ will आता है, और 2nd/3rd Person (You, He, They) के साथ shall आता है:
    • "You shall not move." (आदेश: तुम हिलोगे नहीं)।
    • "They shall be rewarded." (वादा: उन्हें पुरस्कार दिया जाएगा)।
    • "I will crack SSC CGL 2026." (दृढ़ संकल्प: मैं परीक्षा पास करूँगा ही)।

7. Perfect Continuous Tenses & The 'Since vs For' Rule7. पूर्ण चालू काल एवं 'Since बनाम For' का सटीक नियम

Perfect Continuous Tenses describe an action that started in the past and is still continuing into the present or up to a specified time frame.

  • Present Perfect Continuous: S + has/have been + V-ing + (since/for + time)
    "She has been suffering from fever for two days."
  • Past Perfect Continuous: S + had been + V-ing + (since/for + time)
    "She had been playing chess the whole day yesterday."

The Definitive Rule: Since vs For

  • SINCE (Point of Time): Used when the exact starting point of the action is named:
    • Specific days/dates: since Monday, since 15th August, since 2004
    • Parts of day: since morning, since noon, since evening, since night
    • Stages of life / Events: since childhood, since his birth, since I arrived here
    • Clock time: since 8:00 AM, since 4 o'clock
  • FOR (Period / Duration of Time): Used for counting numerical duration:
    • Number + units: for two hours, for ten days, for five months, for three years, for a long time

Since बनाम For का अचूक नियम:

  • SINCE (निश्चित बिंदु-समय / Point of Time): जब काम के शुरू होने का निश्चित समय, दिन, तारीख या पहर दिया हो:
    since Monday (सोमवार से), since 2010 (2010 से), since morning (सुबह से), since childhood (बचपन से), since 5 o'clock (5 बजे से)।
  • FOR (अवधि / Period of Time): जब समय की गिनती या कुल अवधि दी हो:
    for two days (दो दिन से), for five hours (पाँच घंटे से), for ten years (दस साल से), for a long time (काफी समय से)।

1. What is a Tense? (Time vs State of Action)

A Tense is defined as that form of a verb which indicates two fundamental dimensions:

  1. The Time of an Action: When the action takes place (Present, Past, or Future).
  2. The State / Aspect of an Action: How the action exists (habitual, in progress, fully completed, or continuing over a period of time).

(A) Time of an Action:

  • Present: He goes to school. (Action relates to present time).
  • Past: He went to school. (Action relates to past time).
  • Future: He will go to school. (Action relates to future time).

(B) State / Function of an Action:

  • Habitual (Indefinite): I write letters regularly. (General habit).
  • Progressive (Continuous): I am writing a letter. (Ongoing action right now).
  • Preceding (Perfect): I have just written a letter. (Completed before now, connected to present).
  • Time Expression (Perfect Continuous): I have been writing a letter for two hours. (Began in past, still continuing).

⏱️ The 3 Time Frames / समय के तीन ढाँचे:
1. Point of Time: A specific exact moment (e.g., in 1947, on Monday, at 7:00 PM).
2. Period of Time: A duration without fixed start point (e.g., for ten years, from Monday to Saturday).
3. Expression of Time: Combination of point and duration (e.g., winter 1950, since childhood).

2. The Present Indefinite Tense (Simple Present)

Basic Sentence Structure:

  • Affirmative: Subject + V1 (s/es with 3rd person singular) + Object
  • Negative: Subject + do/does not + V1 + Object
  • Interrogative: Do/Does + Subject + V1 + Object?

Core Usages:

  1. Habits, Customs, Routines & Repeated Actions: Expressed with Adverbs of Frequency: often, seldom, usually, never, occasionally, sometimes, normally, generally, always, frequently, rarely, daily.
    Example: "The old lady goes for a walk in the morning daily." / "Suhani always comes in time."
  2. Permanent Nature & Eternal Scientific Principles (Universal Truths):
    Example: "Water boils at 100°C." / "Rivers freeze at high altitude." / "Plants prepare their own food."
  3. Historical Present (Dramatic Narration): Used by commentators and storytellers to make past events vivid.
    Example: "Now Netaji enters and addresses the Indian soldiers."
  4. Fixed Future Arrangement / Timetable: Official schedules and planned future events.
    Example: "The Prime Minister arrives from New York tomorrow." / "He leaves for his new job next week."

3. Present Continuous Tense & The Stative Verbs Master List

Structure: Subject + is/am/are + V-ing + Object

Primary Functions:

  • Action in Progress: Action happening at the moment of speaking (temporary nature): "It is raining outside." / "She is swimming in the river."

Stative vs Progressive: Contrast of Meaning

Some verbs can be used in the -ing form ONLY when their meaning shifts from a state to an active physical action:

  • Smell (State): The rose smells sweet. (गुलाब की खुशबू मीठी है — Stative)
    Smell (Active Action): She is smelling a black rose. (वह काला गुलाब सूँघ रही है — Progressive)
  • Have (Possession): She has a large house. (उसके पास बड़ा घर है — Stative)
    Have (Eating/Action): She is having lunch now. (वह अभी खाना खा रही है — Progressive)
  • Think (Opinion): I think she is honest. (मुझे लगता है वह ईमानदार है — Stative)
    Think (Mental Planning): I am thinking of moving to Delhi. (मैं दिल्ली जाने की योजना बना रहा हूँ — Progressive)

4. Present Perfect Tense & The 2 Cardinal Rules

Structure: Subject + has/have + V3 + Object

The Present Perfect Tense represents an action completed in the past that has a direct, active link with the present moment.

Common Signal Adverbs: ever, just, already, recently, lately, yet, so far, till now, by the time.

  • "I have just finished my breakfast." (अभी-अभी खाया है).
  • "We have seen this movie already." (पहले ही देख चुके हैं).
  • "We haven't seen Reeta lately." (इधर हाल में नहीं देखा).

Golden Rule 1: Present Perfect + Definite Past Point of Time = SIMPLE PAST

If a sentence contains a definite finished point of time in the past (such as yesterday, two days ago, last year, in 1947, the other day, formerly), you MUST use Simple Past (V2), NEVER Present Perfect (has/have + V3)!

Top Recurring SSC Questions:

  • ✗ She has returned two days ago. (Incorrect — omit 'has')
    ✓ She returned two days ago. (Correct — Simple Past)
  • ✗ I have met your brother yesterday. (Incorrect — omit 'have')
    ✓ I met your brother yesterday. (Correct)
  • ✗ India has won independence in 1947. (Incorrect)
    ✓ India won independence in 1947. (Correct)

Golden Rule 2: Present Indefinite + Time Expression = PRESENT PERFECT

When a state or action started in the past and continues into the present with since, for, how long, whole, all along, you cannot use Simple Present; you MUST use Present Perfect!

  • ✗ He knows me for two years. (Wrong)
    ✓ He has known me for two years. (Correct)
  • ✗ She owns this parlour since 2002. (Wrong)
    ✓ She has owned this parlour since 2002. (Correct)

5. Past Tenses & Past Perfect (The 'Past of the Past' Rule)

A. Past Indefinite (Simple Past): Subject + V2 + Object

  • Used for completed past actions with past time markers: "She bought a car two years ago."
  • Used for past habits: "He always carried an umbrella." / "I used to go to Delhi by train."

B. Past Continuous: Subject + was/were + V-ing + Object

  • Action in progress in the past: "It was still raining when I reached there."

C. Past Perfect (had + V3):

Past Perfect does NOT simply mean past; it means the earlier of two past actions!

The Two Past Actions Formula (Before / After)

1st Action (Earlier) → Past Perfect [had + V3]
2nd Action (Later) → Simple Past [V2]
  • ✓ The patient had died before the doctor arrived.
  • ✓ The train had left before we reached the station.
  • ✓ I finished the book after I had returned from college.
  • ⚡ Single Action Blunder: Never use Past Perfect for a single standalone past action without an earlier reference point!
    ✗ I had gone to Delhi last week. (Incorrect)
    ✓ I went to Delhi last week. (Correct — Simple Past)

Unfulfilled Wishes / Intentions with Past Perfect

When verbs like want, hope, expect, think, suppose, intend are used with had + V3, it indicates that the action was desired or planned, but DID NOT take place!

  • ✓ I had wanted to help my brother. (Meaning: but I could not help).
  • ✓ I had expected to pass the exam. (Meaning: but I did not pass).
  • ✓ Vishal had intended to set up his own business. (Meaning: but could not).

6. Future Tenses & The Nuance of Shall vs Will

Structure:

  • Future Indefinite: Subject + will/shall + V1 (They will come here shortly).
  • Future Continuous: Subject + will/shall be + V-ing (She will be waiting for me when I reach).
  • Future Perfect: Subject + will/shall have + V3 (She will have prepared food before I reach home).

The Shall vs Will Rule (Normal vs Emphatic/Modal):

  • Ordinary / Neutral Future: Use Shall with 1st Person (I, We); Use Will with 2nd & 3rd Person (You, He, She, They).
  • Determination, Promise, Threat, Order, or Official Duty: The rule is REVERSED!
    • Use Will with I, We (e.g., "I will help my brother." — Firm determination).
    • Use Shall with You, He, They (e.g., "You shall not move." — Strict order; "They shall be rewarded." — Solemn promise).

7. Perfect Continuous Tenses & The 'Since vs For' Rule

Perfect Continuous Tenses describe an action that started in the past and is still continuing into the present or up to a specified time frame.

  • Present Perfect Continuous: S + has/have been + V-ing + (since/for + time)
    "She has been suffering from fever for two days."
  • Past Perfect Continuous: S + had been + V-ing + (since/for + time)
    "She had been playing chess the whole day yesterday."

The Definitive Rule: Since vs For

  • SINCE (Point of Time): Used when the exact starting point of the action is named:
    • Specific days/dates: since Monday, since 15th August, since 2004
    • Parts of day: since morning, since noon, since evening, since night
    • Stages of life / Events: since childhood, since his birth, since I arrived here
    • Clock time: since 8:00 AM, since 4 o'clock
  • FOR (Period / Duration of Time): Used for counting numerical duration:
    • Number + units: for two hours, for ten days, for five months, for three years, for a long time

Practice Question 1
She _______ from London two days ago. (ago = definite past point of time)
A returned
B has returned
C had returned
D was returning
Practice Question 2
Mr. Sharma _______ this luxury showroom since 2010. (since + time expression with stative verb)
A has owned
B is owning
C has been owning
D owns
Practice Question 3
व्याकरण की दृष्टि से अशुद्ध वाक्य पहचानें:
A This ancestral property is belonging to my family.
B This ancestral property belongs to my family.
C She is having lunch with her client right now.
D The soup smells delicious.
Practice Question 4
The train _______ the station before we reached the platform. (Past of the past)
A had left
B left
C has left
D was leaving
Practice Question 5
I _______ him well for more than five years. (know = stative verb with 'for')
A have known
B am knowing
C have been knowing
D know
Practice Question 6
Water _______ at 100 degrees Celsius. (Universal scientific truth)
A boils
B is boiling
C has boiled
D boiled
Practice Question 7
She _______ for her lost passport since morning. (action ongoing from morning)
A has been searching
B is searching
C searched
D had searched
Practice Question 8
I _______ to assist him financially, but my own salary was delayed. (Unfulfilled past wish)
A had wanted
B wanted
C have wanted
D was wanting
Practice Question 9

A shall
B will
C would
D may

A for
B since
C from
D by

B will land

D often get
